assertions.text: `--local-only` disables pushes and PRs but is explicitly not an OS or network sandbox, since story agents can execute arbitrary shell commands; a hard no-push boundary requires removing git remotes.

Merges are blocked behind fail-closed gates: declared tests, build-before-commit, an evidence critic judging captured command output, and write-surface ownership; the human reviews a PR the gates already accepted.

A cloud option runs the same fleet on a hosted site with isolated sandboxes and provider keys, or users can attach their own machine as a cloud runner via `baro login` and `baro connect --install-service`.
The tool requires Node 20+, git, and at least one LLM backend: the claude CLI (default), codex, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; `baro --doctor` checks the setup.

Flags include backend selection (--llm claude|codex|openai|opencode|pi|hybrid|jigjoy), model override, effort level, parallel agent count, execution mode, --quick, --local-only, per-command shell budget, custom OpenAI base URL, and per-tier backend mapping.

CLI commands include headless detached runs printing a run id, `watch` and `logs` for following runs, `runs`/`stop` for listing and stopping, `--resume` (never re-plans), `--continue` (always re-plans), `--doctor`, `login`, and `connect`.
The architecture is described as a Rust TUI host plus a TypeScript orchestrator whose bounded contexts communicate over the Mozaik event bus, with machine gates in front of every merge.

Goals are compiled by an architect into machine-checkable invariants before coding, split into a DAG of stories built in parallel across isolated git worktrees, with runtime replanning able to add and rewire stories mid-run and failed gates spawning remediation stories.

The product is installed globally via npm as baro-ai and is invoked as `baro "<goal>"` inside a repository, opening a TUI where intake asks questions, the user confirms the plan, and the run proceeds.

Codex, OpenCode, and Pi workers are one-shot CLI processes that cannot consume corrective messages after exit; failed verdicts for those backends require a separate recovery execution rather than in-process revision.

The runtime is distributed but not leaderless: the Board serializes scheduling and durable graph commits while separate participants own goal meaning, route selection, lease granting, quality evaluation, merging, and verification.

The docs state Baro lacks a trusted per-story CandidateVerifier that executes new deterministic commands in the active worktree, so genuinely missing or fully stale command evidence stays inconclusive after bounded rechecks.
jigjoy-ai/baro is mentioned in this evidence.

Repository development practice: the experiment guide instructs preparing a clean git repo with an unexecuted prd.json whose stories have concrete acceptance criteria and test commands, and installing workspace dependencies with npm install before running trials.
`--local-only` disables pushes and PRs but is explicitly not an OS or network sandbox, since story agents can execute arbitrary shell commands; a hard no-push boundary requires removing git remotes.

Codex, OpenCode, and Pi workers are one-shot CLI processes that cannot consume corrective messages after exit; failed verdicts for those backends require a separate recovery execution rather than in-process revision.
Collective coordination is the CLI default; a legacy Conductor mode (one owner of DAG levels, retries, completion) can be selected with `--coordination legacy` for A/B comparison.

Runtime replan proposals carry run/story/lease/generation and a graphVersion; invalid, stale, cyclic, unauthorized, over-budget or non-durable candidates get a correlated rejection and are never shown as applied just because a model requested them.

The public CLI does not yet expose process-level run resumption: a restart creates a new run identity, keeps the graph version as baseline, resets the discovery budget, and does not expose the old decision ledger.

A paired A/B harness (ab-run.ts) compares legacy vs collective coordination on identical PRD bytes across isolated clones, alternating arm order, hashing verify inputs, and producing per-trial artifacts including diff.patch, metrics.json, and audit logs.

In collective mode, workers publish credential-free capabilities and bids, a broker grants a correlated lease to a deterministic winner, and with the Critic enabled a story passes only after the acceptance verdict plus StoryMerged, not merely when the model process exits.

Proposal IDs act as idempotency keys: exact re-delivery returns the remembered decision without reapplying, reuse with different content is rejected, and applied decisions can be restored from the PRD's runtimeGraph metadata when a host resumes the same runId.

The DialogueAgent is text-only with no codebase tools; it may send a bounded targeted message and one add-only delegation proposal of at most two stories, with no authority over removal, rewiring, priority, retries, model, route, lease, or merging.
